headline: Majors hold the 200-day line while momentum cools; whale demand reverses after three weeks of supply, but positioning stays crowded and expensive.
paragraphs: All seven majors sit above their 200-day moving average, and five of them have already crossed above the 50-day, but the picture is not one of clean uptrend. Bitcoin is up 24.2% on the month and up 0.1% on the day, but down 0.5% on the week. Ethereum mirrors the same tension: up 33.0% on the month, up 0.5% on the day, down 0.8% on the week. Solana is worse: up 42.2% on the month, up 2.7% on the day, but down 3.0% on the week. Cardano is the only asset where all three windows agree in the same direction, climbing 0.7% on the day, 2.8% on the week, and 33.5% on the month. The regime is one of strong medium-term lift meeting recent pullback; the 200-day hold is real, but the week-to-day reversal across the board tells you the crowd is testing that floor, not advancing from it.

Momentum diverges from trend across the majors in ways that matter. Bitcoin and Ethereum both sit in the 60s on RSI-14 (66.9 and 64.7, respectively) with MACD below signal line, a classic setup where the move has run into resistance and the mechanical impulse has gone flat. Solana and XRP show the same: high RSI (67.5, 61.1) but MACD below signal. Only Binance breaks the pattern with RSI at 71.0 and MACD above signal, suggesting it alone has not lost upside momentum. Cardano and Dogecoin both have MACD above signal but modest RSI (60.4, 62.0), meaning the turn is early and the crowd has not yet crowded in. The read is straightforward: Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana have run their rallies hard, cooled into overbought RSI, and are now resting while smaller caps or secondary players take the baton. None of this means reversal; it means the daily tailwind has shifted to sideways.

Funding and open interest reveal a market where leverage is expensive and longs are crowded. Bitcoin funding runs at 0.0031% per 8 hours (3.4% annualized), Ethereum at 0.0038% (4.2%), and all majors except Solana are positive, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold. Solana sits at minus 0.0032% (negative 3.5%), a rare sight that says shorts are paying longs, a signal that the smart money may be hedging against further upside there. Open interest in Bitcoin is 2.1 billion dollars, Ethereum 1.48 billion; these are not trivial pools. The long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin is 1.07 (near parity), but on Ethereum it is 1.31 and on Solana it rises to 1.73, meaning the leverage is increasingly tilted long as you move down the cap curve. Dogecoin shows 3.56 longs per short, a heavily positioned bet. In the last 10 hours, Bitcoin has liquidated 100 positions with 964,000 dollars in long liquidations versus only 53,000 in shorts, a 18-to-1 ratio. Ethereum, in the last 2 hours, flipped: 4,983 dollars in long liquidations but 784,000 in shorts. Solana's 5-hour window shows 1.07 million in longs liquidated versus 179,000 in shorts. The liquidation tape is messy and the window is short for each, but the pattern across Bitcoin and Solana points to longs getting shaken at resistance.

Whale behavior has reversed sharply in the last 48 hours. Over the three weeks ending August 30, big players moved 441 million, then 946 million, then 775 million dollars onto exchanges, a clear supply imprint. In the week ending September 6, the direction flipped: 494 million dollars moved off exchanges, the first weekly net withdrawal in the window. The two-day picture amplifies this: Bitcoin saw 99.6 million dollars leave exchanges, with 154.6 million flowing out from Coinbase Institutional and 51.5 million each from two separate Coinbase Institutional addresses. Offsetting this were 55 million into OKX and 120 million plus 100 million in stablecoin inflows to Bitfinex and Binance respectively. The message is layered: Bitcoin whales are consolidating off-exchange while traditional-finance stablecoin is moving into centralized venues, likely ahead of ETF rebalancing or institutional entry. Spot ETF flows on Bitcoin were 174.6 million dollars on September 4 and 986.7 million net positive over the last five sessions, with three consecutive days in the same direction. Ethereum ETF flows are smaller (25.9 million on the day, 215.3 million over five sessions) but consistent. The stablecoin float stands at 310.6 billion dollars, up 1.45% on the month, stable dry powder.

Fear and Greed sits at 73, in the Greed regime, though it has ranged as low as 27 in the past 30 days, telling you the crowd has cycled through hard doubt. The total market cap fell 3.36% on the day to 2.7 trillion, while Bitcoin dominance actually rose to 59.2%, meaning the selloff was distributed, not concentrated. Top movers show schizophrenia: RAY, ARB, and JUP are up 60%, 28%, and 22% respectively, while lower-cap names like SPX and FF are down 6% and 4%. This is a market where strength exists in pockets, not across the board.

What to watch: Bitcoin's hold above 79,000 and the 200-day moving average, which has become the line in the sand after the week of pullback. If the 200-day is reclaimed with MACD turning back above signal and funding remains positive but does not spike further, the rest could be momentum consolidation rather than reversal. Conversely, if whale accumulation continues off-exchange while ETF flows stay net positive, the signal is that big money is confident enough to take physical custody, a structural shift worth noting. The Ethereum and Bitcoin liquidation asymmetry over the last few hours is too short a window to be decisive, but if it persists with longs continuing to cascade, the momentum divergence becomes a sell signal rather than a simple rest.
